To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

histone deacylation and DNA methyaltion are associated with silening of gene expression from CMV promoter in parental AAVP and inhibitors of histone decetylases boost gene exression from Grp78 promoter of dual tumor-targeted hybrid AAVP in cancer cells.

the combination of the histone deacylase inhibitor drugs, and the Grp78 tumor-specific promoter in the AAVP, improves gene expression in cancer, and should be considered as a strategy for AAVP-guidance of cancer gene therapy.
inhibition of histone deacetlyation and DNA methylation improves gene expression mediated by the adeno-associated virus/phage (AAVP) in cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a novel AAV/phages vector, which has the ability to specifically target cancer cells in vivo.
the development of a novel AAV/phge hybrid vector (AAVP) for targeted gene delivery to cancer cells.
the development of novel AAVP vectors for cancer gene therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of histone-deacetylation inhibitors and the Grp78 tumor-specific promoter improves AAVP gene transfer in cancer cells and that cell confluence state has no effect on AAvP gene expression.
the Grp78 tumor-specific promoter and histone deacylase inhibitors can be used to improve AAV-mediated gene therapy in cancer cells.
inhibition of histone deacylation and DNA methyaltion is associated with improved gene expression mediated by AAVP in cancer cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the combination of histone acetylation and DNA demethylation improves AAVP gene transfer in cancer cells.

we designed a new vector that targets cancer cells, and we have now shown that we can improve gene expression in cancer by combining a stress-inducible promoter and an inhibitor of histone deacylation.

we have developed an improved phage-based gene therapy vector that can specifically deliver therapeutic genes into tumors and we have shown that histone deactivation is a key factor for gene expression from the phage-based vector in cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AAVP-based gene expression is associated with histone deacethylation and DNA methylation.
the AAVP system has the potential to be used for cancer gene therapy and can be improved by using histone deacelylase inhibitors to boost the gene expression mediated by the AAVP.
the combination of a histone deacylase inhibitor and a stress-inducible promoter is a promising strategy for improving AAVP-mediated systemic gene delivery in cancer.
